doc: The first-match tutorial (scripts/match/tutorial.gd, TutorialCamps): eight beats (DECISIONS 2026-11-08). The hunter lands at level 1 with one ability point and every ability locked, the same as a real run; a beat that uses an ability unlocks it on its own (Tutorial.UNLOCKS, with the level it needs), and each camp's kills pay the XP for the next level (camps: the step that spawns it, its monsters, the level its last kill reaches, 0 for none; row = in a line in front of you; hp = its own share of the monster's health in place of camp_hp). Spending points, ranks, wall kicks, crouching and gloves are one-time hints in the first matches (FirstMatchGuide, ExpeditionTips), not beats. steps: [id, the one banner line]. Two beats run in legs (Tutorial.leg): dash crosses the three gaps (dash, exdash, glide), extract walks to the outpost, starts the uplink, holds it and takes the lift (wayout, uplink, defend, extract); a leg's line is its alt line. detail: a plain-words second line under it (per beat or leg; %L the step's ability in the kit's own words, %X the E ability in words, %R the rank-up keys, %N the E ability's name, %U the ultimate's level, %F interact). %K the step's own key (its cap), %Y the Ultimate's key (R) and %Z its name (the Fusion is the ultimate key, X), %J jump, %G glide, %E the E key, %T the Boki key, %s the Boki's name, %A the step's ability name; the step's key shows as a key cap beside the line. alt: the line for a variant of a step or a leg. labels: the marker's caption per step or leg. mob: how the tutorial's monsters differ from real ones (camp_hp times the health, so the kills come quickly; size up, damage and attack tempo down). cds: the share of its usual time every ability, dash and glove cooldown takes here. need: how many times a step's action must land, shown as 1/3 on the pill. 'wayout' is the Ways Out hook: the leg the limited-ways-out work swaps for its own exit beat. retry: the one line shown when you fall into the abyss and the beat (or leg) starts again (same tokens; default for the ones without one).

tips.stun: Stunned: no moving, attacks or dash for a moment
tips.root: Rooted: no walking or dash for a moment, but you can still fight
tips.grounded: Grounded: no dash or jump for a moment

steps: Press %K to send %s at the monsters
Press %K at the chest to open it
Step into the light to leave

detail.glide: A tap just flicks it: keep %J held until you are across.
detail.shoot_draw: Hold the button to draw the bow, let go to loose. A longer draw hits harder.
detail.shoot_melee: Walk up close and tap to swing. Hold to charge a wave.
detail.gkey: %T sends %s at a monster; tap again to recall %s.
detail.summon: %s bursts out and fights for %D seconds: watch the ring
detail.summon_back: Back to a light. %s rests now.
detail.summon_knocked: %s got beaten and flew back to you. It needs a longer rest.
detail.uplink: Stay in the circle, or the capture slips back.
detail.defend: Stay in the circle, or the capture slips back.
detail.kin: They stand in a row: line them up, then use it.
detail.dash: Every gap is a different move: dash, air dash, then glide.
detail.chest: Chests take a key; monsters with a key glint carry them.
detail.extract: A match has few ways out; this one is at the outpost.

alt.summon_early: That calls it back early: let it stay
alt.shoot_draw: Hold %K to draw, let go to loose
alt.shoot_melee: Step in and swing at them (%K)
alt.wayout: Few ways out: walk to the outpost
alt.defend: Defend the outpost: stay in the circle

retry.default: Back at your last stop. Try again
retry.dash: Back at your last stop. Dash from the glowing pad
retry.exdash: Back at your last stop. Jump from the pad, then dash
retry.glide: Back at your last stop. Jump, press %J again to glide
retry.shoot: Back at your last stop. Fight with solid ground behind you
retry.gkey: Back at your last stop. Tap %T and let %s go in first
retry.summon: Back at your last stop. Press %M and let %s out first
retry.kin: Back at your last stop. Line them up, then use %A
retry.fight: Back at your last stop. Use %A with solid ground behind you

lead_doc: Your Boki leads on the steps with a lead goal (TutorialLead): it runs ahead to the goal, waits when you are more than wait_m behind, stops stop_m from it and looks back at you. It sprints at run_speed m/s (a wisp floats at wisp_speed) so it can be ahead of a running Hunter; a Boki you have passed just falls in beside you, and one that stood stalled for stall_s s trying to lead (an edge or a wall on the straight way) falls in beside you for off_s s, then leads again.
